messages:
maria: FYI support escalation from Acme. Customer hit a big burst around 10:12Z and got 502/504s for ~2m. We see scale-up lag on hosted inference (HPA+KEDA). Posting quick notes and logs below.

josh: ack — can you paste the gateway logs and scaledobject?

maria: Gateway snippet: 
```
[10:12:19] upstream request failed: no backend ready -> 504
[10:12:23] upstream request failed: connection reset by peer
[10:13:02] downstream timeout after 30s -> 502
```
ScaledObject + HPA: 
```
ScaledObject: acme-tenant-model-runner
triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      query: |-
        sum(rate(kafka_consumer_lag[30s])) by (tenant)
cooldownPeriod: 300
minReplicaCount: 0
maxReplicaCount: 8
HPA: minReplicas: 0 -> targetCPU: 60%
```
Observation: KEDA cooldown=300 + scale-to-zero (minReplicas 0) + long model init -> obvious warmup hole.

sam: Do we have model-init durations? If init ~40-60s and readiness probe waits longer, combined with pod scheduling + image pull could be >60s.

maria: Model init times from logs: 
```
[model-init] load weights start -> 18s
[model-init] quantize load -> 12s
[kv-cache warm] first request priming -> 22s
Total ~52s before ready, but scheduling adds 8-15s under node pressure. Heartbeat logs show pod didn't register as ready for ~75s.
```

leah: KEDA + HPA interplay: with minReplicas:0 we need to rely on ScaledObject trigger detection and then KEDA will create an HPA which then scales pods. That detection + cooldown can add 10-30s. If cooldown 300s, it suppresses rapid new scaling? Also I think our readiness probe threshold (concurrency=1) waits for a warm prefix that we don't have.

josh: Repro steps I ran in staging: 
1) set minReplicas:0 and scaledobject cooldown 300
2) fire 200 concurrent requests over 10s: `hey -n 200 -c 50 http://staging/generate`
3) observed 30s of 502/504s then gradual recovery as pods came up.

maria: Relevant PromQL: 
```
sum(rate(redwood_gateway_request_duration_seconds_count[1m])) by (code)
and
kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace="inference"}
```
We saw readiness drop and activation lag spike aligned with request errors.

sam: Quick mitigation for customer: bump minReplicaCount to 1 for their tenant pool to avoid scale-to-zero. Also reduce KEDA cooldown to 30s and set HPA minReplicas:1.

leah: Agreed. Also we should add a prewarm lifecycle: keep a tiny warm cache or fast-start image. For immediate fix I'll apply minReplica=1 and smaller cooldown for the tenant.

maria: I've applied a temporary change to their Dedicated pool: minReplicaCount -> 1 and KEDA cooldown -> 30. Monitoring now.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4531 severity=high assigned=eng-oncall owner=leah

josh: Customer update?

maria: Support told customer we applied a config change and to expect improved success rates. They saw errors stop after ~90s. No billing break found. Auth tokens were fine.

sam: Action items: 
- leah: follow up with infra to reduce cold-start time (image layer caching + prewarm hook)
- josh: run load-repro in prod-canary and capture detailed pod startup traces (cgroups, node pressure)
- maria: coordinate customer postmortem and confirm SLA impact
- ops: consider default minReplicaCount=1 for small-tenants with predictable burst patterns OR provide a recommended template.

leah: I'll open a repo issue for warm-start improvements (pin images to layers, init container to fetch weights into local volume) and add a KEDA docs note about cooldown vs model init.

maria: tagging here for visibility: @leah @josh @sam. Closing loop: keep this thread for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

josh: quick note — avoid changing cooldown globally; we should target tenant-level overrides. KEDA scales are noisy if we lower cooldown everywhere.

maria: noted. We'll keep scoped change. Closing for now, will attach postmortem when ready.
